threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Stoke Newington Church Street' instead of just 'the Church Street' like everyone else here.
Saw a lad playing his sax on the 21 last night—bus driver stopped the whole thing just to listen, like we were in a jazz club for a moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The aroma of grilled corn wafting from the market on Hermannplatz while a neighbor argues passionately with a street musician—that’s when I knew.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a late-night tram here with DJ sets onboard. It's like a rolling party—only in Berlin do you ride along to live beats while cruising the streets.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: If they know which taco truck to hit after midnight, they’re local. If they say 'taco' instead of 'tacos,' they’re definitely just here for a gig.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus while discussing the latest BART delays. Classic SF—chaos mixed with creativity, even when transit's a mess.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the parks and plazas, but the real charm lies in the tiny, tucked-away bars where the locals laugh until dawn.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their confused looks while trying to navigate the metro map—especially when they attempt to pronounce 'L2'.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still go to Broadway Market on Saturdays like it’s a novelty, rather than just your go-to for overpriced avocado toast.
Last night, the 133 stopped to let on a guy with a full saxophone. He played a solo the whole way to Camberwell, we were all just vibing.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a guy practicing opera in the park while his dog chased pigeons. That’s Neukölln for you—chaos meets creativity.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find the spontaneous street concerts on random corners, where locals just whip out instruments and jam in the sunset.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to avoid BART during rush hour after a smoke scare—no one who's just working here would bother.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a street performer on the 49 bus today. He used the handrail like a mic stand, belting out oldies. Only in SF do you get a concert with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists don’t realize that the best tapas spots aren’t on Carrer Gran de Gràcia but tucked away on tiny side streets. Big difference.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their tendency to ask for 'una tapa de patatas bravas' at every bar, instead of just 'bravas'.
